review_notes: Reviewed all 132 lines of BranchSeparation.lean and read the relevant imports and neighboring files, especially BranchCoupling.lean, CounterexampleAssembly.lean, CoulombEstimates.lean, CompactSeparation.lean, BranchInterfaces.lean, ComponentRegions.lean, SmoothBranchMarginal.lean and ActualGeometryConclusion.lean. The only substantial repeated proof machinery found is the branchMarginal support-transport argument, which is essentially line-for-line repeated in CounterexampleAssembly.lean. I checked that CounterexampleAssembly.lean does not import BranchSeparation.lean and that its direct low-level dependencies also do not import BranchSeparation.lean, so the cited proof is independent rather than a wrapper around the target. I did not execute Lean; the proposed refactor is a proof sketch and has not been compiled. Transitive imports were not exhaustively traversed, though the direct dependency chain inspected shows no cycle risk.

    filter_upwards [hnu] with x hx

findings.problem: This proof re-derives the generic support-transport theorem for branchMarginal: it unfolds the central-plus-four-pushforward decomposition, splits using ae_add_measure_iff, handles the 1/3 and 1/6 smul weights, and pushes membership through each measurable H i with ae_map_iff. The same nontrivial argument already appears as Problem356.ae_branchMarginal_mem in CounterexampleAssembly.lean, lines 25-40, with U arbitrary and B=K, U=⋃ i, components K H i as a special case. The target theorem is therefore a specialization, but its proof duplicates the whole measure-algebra block instead of invoking the general result. CounterexampleAssembly.lean does not import BranchSeparation.lean, so this is an independent duplicate proof, not a wrapper around the target.
findings.proposed_change: Move or generalize Problem356.ae_branchMarginal_mem from CounterexampleAssembly.lean into BranchCoupling.lean, the file that defines branchMarginal, keeping its general statement. Then replace the target proof block with the specialization: obtain hcompact := isCompact_iUnion (compact_components hK hcont), apply ae_branchMarginal_mem nu hH hcompact.measurableSet hnu, prove central membership by mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨0, hx⟩, and prove outer membership by mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨i.succ, mem_image_of_mem _ hx⟩. Both BranchSeparation.lean and CounterexampleAssembly.lean already import BranchCoupling.lean, so neither needs a new heavy import. The theorem statement remains unchanged.
findings.benefit: One proof of the branchMarginal support decomposition would serve both the assembly file and the branch-separation file. The target theorem becomes a short specialization, eliminating the risk that the two copies drift when branchMarginal is refactored, and the general support API would live with the measure it describes rather than in a high-level assembly file.
